note: Forest, glades and bottomland fields along the east bank of the Little Niangua River in eastern Hickory County. MDC's two primitive camping spots are on side-by-side spurs south off County Road 96 just east of the river: the west spur is a gravel lane along a mown strip with the area's privy, ending in a turnaround; the east spur is a grass two-track into the trees. No water or other facilities. --Claude
summary: Confirmed: two map/GIS-designated primitive camping spots on adjacent spurs off County Road 96 (GIS 56 and 1044, 155 m apart), one privy. Free/FCFS/no hookups/14 nights now manual. Phone matches; not waterfront kept. Pin is on the minor (east, two-track) spur; the west spur with the gravel lane and privy is the main camp.
flags: INCLUSION OK: area page 'Things to Do: Camping: Designated Camping Sites' and 'Camping is allowed only in spots designated on the area map... There is a privy located at the designated camping area'; brochure (07/2023) 'Primitive camping is permitted only in spots designated on the area map'; the map (Last Updated 1/30/2026) has two 'Camping Area' symbols side by side south of CR 96 with the Privy symbol beside them; GIS 27 points 56 and 1044 'Primitive Camping Area'. Rule 140 standard; no special-use-only rule, no Rule 101.

PIN (optional 140 m move to the main camp): stored 37.99040,-93.09330 = GIS 1044, at the end of a grass two-track that leaves CR 96 ~90 m to the NW and runs into open trees (no gravel, no pad visible). GIS 56 (37.98980,-93.09489, 155 m WSW) is at the turnaround at the end of a ~130 m gravel lane through a mown strip, with the privy on a small gravel apron halfway down (about 37.99062,-93.09503) and vehicles parked at the turnaround in the imagery. That west spur is the clear main camp; suggested pin 37.99037,-93.09486 on its lane beside the mown strip. One cluster, one entrance road (CR 96): no split.

ACCESS: County Road 96 from Route F crosses the Little Niangua River ~450 m west of the camps on a straight concrete span; imagery cannot tell a bridge from a low-water slab, and neither the map nor the brochure marks a low-water crossing. The camps are also reached from the east (County Roads 66/525) without crossing the river. No 4WD wording, no posted limit. The west spur's gravel lane and turnaround take a 23-ft rig; the east two-track is grass.
WATERFRONT: not waterfront kept. Both spots are ~400-500 m east of the Little Niangua River in upland woods.
HORSES: brochure 'Horseback riding is prohibited.' No horse camp.
PHONE: page '(417) 895-6880' matches stored (the 07/2023 brochure gives the Lebanon office, (417) 532-7612).
FACILITIES: privy at the west camping spur (page, map; not written - vault_toilets could take it by hand).
